Consider the circle of radius $4$ centered at the origin, as shown above. Construct a set of parametric equations, defined for $\theta \in [0,2\pi ),$ that traverse the circle once in the counterclockwise direction starting at the point $A(4,0).$

question.worked_solution:
The parametric equations of a circle of radius $r$ centered at the origin are

$$
x=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).
$$

Under this parametrization, the circle is traversed once in the counterclockwise direction, starting from $(r,0).$

In our case, the radius is $r=4.$ Substituting $r=4$ gives

$$
x=4\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=4\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).
$$
